IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r2.claim: One Qur'anic sense of loss is reduction, as in giving short measure.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r2.anchor: أحدها : النقص . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن : ﴿ وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان ﴾

BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r1.claim: Establishing weight with justice means making it straight; ‘weight’ is knowing a thing’s measure and extends to fairness in all intended acts and words.
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r1.anchor: قوموا وزنكم بالعدل أي اجعلوه مستقيما به وفي المفردات الوزن معرفة قدر الشيء

BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r2.claim: Do not diminish the balance or what it measures: it should be even, the purpose for which it was established; the lexicons distinguish shortchanging from the verb for commercial loss.
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r2.anchor: يقال : خسرت الشيء بالفتح واحسرته نقصته وبابه ضرب

BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r3.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r3.claim: Sa‘di al-Mufti says the command concerns not reducing the weighed goods, not damaging the scale; the passage first requires fairness, then prohibits excess, then shortchanging, and repeats ‘balance’ for emphasis.
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r3.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : المراد لا تنقصوا الموزون في الميزان لا الميزان نفسه

BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r4.claim: Kashifi says the repeated emphasis warns scale users to avoid shame when the Judgment balance is set; his Persian verses say every small or large shortfall and hidden fraud will be exposed.
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي : أين همه تأكيد اهل ترازو راجهت آنست كه بوقت وضع ميزان

BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r5.speaker: مالك بن دينار
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r5.claim: Malik ibn Dinar visited a dying neighbor who described two mountains of fire; the family said he used one measure when giving and another when receiving, and destroying them did not lessen his ordeal.
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r5.anchor: روي عن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله أنه دخل على جار له احتضر فقال

BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r6.claim: Al-Raghib gives two compatible readings: pursue fairness and avoid injustice in weighing, or ensure one’s deeds do not leave the Resurrection balance deficient; Quranic loss concerns the latter, not worldly trade losses.
BURSEVI:v9p238#2/r6.anchor: وفي المفردات قوله : ولا تخسروا الميزان يجوز أن يكون إشارة إلى تحري العدالة

QASHANI:55:8-9/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:8-9/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:8-9/r3.claim: Reducing the balance means falling short of the virtuous mean; a philosopher calls justice God's scale, established among people for truth.
QASHANI:55:8-9/r3.anchor: بالتفريط عن حد الفضيلة. قال بعض الحكماء: العدل ميزان الله تعالى، وضعه للخلق ونصبه للحق.

QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r8.claim: Establish measure with justice by using the standard you would want applied to you, receiving food and drink without short measure.
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r8.anchor: وأقميوا الوزن بالمكيال الذي تحبون أن تكالوا به

SULAMI:v2p293#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p293#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p293#4/r1.claim: Establish unity through truthful outward conduct, a clear interior, a true secret, and firm resolve; be wholly God's and He will be truly yours.
SULAMI:v2p293#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اظهر الوحدانية بصدق الظاهر وصفاء الباطن وحقيقة السر واستقامة العزيمة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#7/r1.claim: القسط means justice, and تخسروا الميزان means reduce the weight.

MAJAZ:v2p242/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p242/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p242/r4.claim: ولا تخسروا means do not wrong people or shortchange the measure; the opposite is fairness and justice.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3322#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3322#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3322#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas saw a man weighing out extra and told him to set the scale's pointer upright, as God commands establishing weight with justice.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3322#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما انه راى رجلا يزن قد ارجح فقال : اقم اللسان كما قال الله : واقيموا الوزن بالقسط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.claim: The word mīzān and the surrounding verbs, prepositions, and qist jointly support both senses; their converging double meanings are a feature of Qur'anic inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.anchor: كل هذه تظاهرت على إفادة هذه المعاني وهذا من إعجاز القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r1.claim: “Establish the weight justly” coordinates with the prohibition if that clause is explanatory, or with “He set the balance” if it gives the rationale.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط } عطف على جملة { ألا تطغوا في الميزان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r2.claim: Iqāma means making something stand, a metaphor for performing it in the fullest intended manner, as with establishing prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r2.anchor: والإقامة : جعل الشيء قائما ، وهو تمثيل للإتيان به على أكمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r3.claim: Weight in its concrete sense balances objects by heaviness, but here includes measuring quantities, volumes, and other measures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r3.anchor: والوزن حقيقته : تحقيق تعادل الأجسام في الثقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r4.claim: Qist means justice; Ibn ʿĀshūr says it is a shortened Arabic form of the Roman-derived qistās, also found in the fuller form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r4.anchor: والقسط : العدل وهو معرب من الرومية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r5.claim: The bāʾ can mark accompaniment, making justice a constant condition of conduct, or causation, requiring justice as the criterion of measurement; compare 6:152 and 5:8.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r5.anchor: والباء للمصاحبة . والمعنى : اجعلوا العدل ملازما لما تقومونه من أموركم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r6.claim: Because pagan merchants practiced short measure, the verse calls it out; “do not diminish the balance” forbids neglecting justice or cheating by weight, depending on the word's sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p239/r6.anchor: وقد كان المشركون يعهدون إلى التطفيف في الوزن كما جاء في قوله تعالى : { ويل للمطففين

NAHHAS:v4p303/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r12.speaker: بلال بن أبي بردة
NAHHAS:v4p303/r12.claim: Bilal ibn Abi Burda reads تخسروا with an open tāʾ, a known dialect form.
NAHHAS:v4p303/r12.anchor: وقرأ بلال بن أبي بردة ( ولا تخسروا ) بفتح التاء وهي لغة معروفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r6.claim: Most readers use أخسر, meaning to cause shortfall or spoil the measure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «ولا تخسروا» من أخسر، أي نقص وأفسد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r7.speaker: بلال بن أبي بردة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r7.claim: Bilal reads خَسِر with open ت and kasra س; both خسر and أخسر mean to reduce or spoil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r7.anchor: وقال بلال بن أبي بردة «تخسروا» بفتح التاء وكسر السين من خسر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r8.speaker: بلال بن أبي بردة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r8.claim: Bilal also has a reading with open ت and س, as Ibn Jinni relates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ بلال أيضا فيما حكى ابن جني: «تخسروا» ، بفتح التاء والسين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#4/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#4/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains not to short the balance as not reducing the weight.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي لا تنقصوا الوزن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r4.claim: He glosses equitable weighing as just weighing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r4.anchor: وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط } أي بالعدل , قال مجاهد : القسط : العدل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r5.claim: Do not diminish the scale by giving short measure; the precise wrong depends on whether الميزان means justice, judgment, or measure.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r5.anchor: ولا تخسروا الميزان } أي لا تنقصوه بالبخس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r6.claim: A further possibility is that the balance is the scale of deeds on Judgment Day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r6.anchor: وفي وجه رابع : أنه ميزان حسناتكم يوم القيامة

MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.claim: Low plants without stems and trees with stems prostrate through their shadows as the sun moves; the sky is raised 500 years above earth, and the balance establishes justice, requiring people not to cheat in measures.
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.anchor: { والنجم } يعني كل نبت ليس له ساق { والشجر } كل نبت له ساق

MUQATIL:55:5-11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r3.claim: “Weigh with justice” means use the balance’s tongue fairly and do not reduce weights; earth is made for creatures, and palm fruits emerge from their coverings like 41:47, including wheat and barley.
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r3.anchor: يعني اللسان بالعدل { ولا تخسروا } يعني ولا تنقصوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#5/r1.claim: Set measures fairly and do not diminish them; the first command forbids short measure and the second also forbids excessive deviation, while repeating الميزان strengthens the instruction.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ﴾ وقوموا وزنكم بالعدل ﴿ ولا تخسروا الميزان ﴾ ولا تنقصوه امر بالتسوية ونهى عن الطغيل الذى هو اعتداء وزيادة

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r10.claim: Establishing the weight means applying it evenly and justly; qist means justice.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r10.anchor: { وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط } أي افعلوه مستقيما بالعدل.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r11.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r11.claim: Abu al-Darda says to set the tongue of the scale straight with justice.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r11.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه: أقيموا لسان الميزان بالقسط والعدل.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r12.speaker: ابن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r12.claim: Ibn ʿUyaynah says the hand establishes the scale while the heart supplies fairness.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عيينة: الإقامة باليد والقسط بالقلب.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r13.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r13.claim: Mujahid says qist, meaning justice, is a borrowing from Roman usage.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r14.claim: Another view compares establishing the weight to performing prayer on time or attending a marketplace, so fair weighing must not be abandoned.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو كقولك أقام الصلاة أي أتى بها في وقتها

QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r1.claim: Not reducing the balance means not diminishing measure or weight, as also stated at 11:84.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r2.claim: Qatadah tells people to act fairly as they want fairness for themselves and to give full measure, since justice sustains society.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة في هذه الآية: اعدل يا بن آدم كما تحب أن يعدل لك، وأوف كما تحب أن يوفى لك

QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r3.claim: Alternatively, the warning means not to diminish one's balance of good deeds on Judgment Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r3.anchor: وقيل: المعنى ولا تخسروا ميزان حسناتكم يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r4.claim: The repetition of “balance” may serve the verse-end rhyme or emphasize full weighing and fairness.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r4.anchor: وكرر الميزان لحال رؤوس الآي. وقيل: التكرير للأمر بإيفاء الوزن

QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r5.claim: The common reading has takhsirū with ḍamma on tāʾ and kasra on sīn; Bilal ibn Abi Burdah and Aban from ʿUthman read with fatha.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r5.anchor: وقراءة العامة «تخسروا» بضم التاء وكسر السين. وقرأ بلال بن أبي بردة وأبان عن عثمان

QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r6.claim: The fatha form is a dialectal alternative; it may also omit the preposition “in.”
QURTUBI-FULL:55:9-12/r6.anchor: وهما لغتان، يقال: أخسرت الميزان وخسرته

SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r1.claim: The common reading uses أخسر with تاء damma and سين kasra, meaning diminish, supported by the verse about short measure.
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r1.anchor:
العامة على ضم التاء وكسر السين من أخسر، أي: نقص كقوله:
وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون

SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r2.claim: He and Bilal ibn Abi Burda read خسر with fatḥa on ت; فعل and أفعل can share the meaning, as in جبر وأجبر.
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وبلال بن أبي بردة بفتح التاء وكسر السين فيكون فعل وأفعل بمعنى

SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r3.claim: An analysis of the open reading deletes a preposition, yielding ولا تخسروا في الميزان.
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r3.anchor: وفيها وجهان، أحدهما: أنه على حذف حرف الجر تقديره: ولا تخسروا في الميزان

SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r4.claim: He objects that no preposition need be omitted because خسر can take an object directly, as in the cited verses.
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r4.anchor:
إلا أن الشيخ قال: " لا حاجة إلى ذلك؛ لأن " خسر " جاء متعديا. قال تعالى:
خسروا أنفسهم

SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r5.claim: The author rejects the examples as semantically different: they mean suffering loss, whereas this verse means making the weighed goods come up short.
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r5.anchor: قلت: وهذا ليس من ذاك. ألا ترى أن { خسروا أنفسهم } { وخسر الدنيا والآخرة } معناه: أن الخسران واقع بهما

SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r6.claim: The reading with fatḥa or ḍamma on سين may be formed by deleting في and joining the verb to its object; خسر has both vowel variants.
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r6.anchor: وقرىء " تخسروا " بفتح التاء وضم السين. قال الزمخشري: " وقرىء ولا تخسروا

SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r7.claim: The noun الميزان is repeated instead of replaced with a pronoun to strengthen its importance; poetry illustrates the same rhetorical repetition.
SAMIN-DURR:55:9/r7.anchor:
وكرر لفظ الميزان، ولم يضمره في الجملتين بعده تقوية لشأنه وهذا كقوله:
4170 لا أرى الموت

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r1.claim: “Establish the weight with justice” explains the previous command: do not exceed the balance by departing from its just establishment.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r1.anchor: هو بمعنى لا تطغوا في الوزن

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r2.claim: One parsing takes aqīmū to mean maintain it continually, as in the command to uphold prayer; the verb may take a preposition or be made transitive with the hamza.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r2.anchor: أقيموا بمعنى قوموا به كما في قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r3.claim: Another parsing equates aqīmū with qawwimū, “make straight,” as one straightens a piece of wood.

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r4.claim: Qisṭ is a noun rather than a verbal noun; adding the hamza in aqsaṭa establishes justice, whereas qaṣaṭa denotes deviation from proper fairness.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r4.anchor: القسط اسم ليس بمصدر ، والأسماء التي

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r5.claim: Thus al-aqsaṭ in “more just” derives semantically from muqsiṭ, which restores the root's justice, rather than from qāsiṭ, which is unjust; comparatives normally use the root form.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#5/r5.anchor: والحاصل أن الأقسط وإن كان نظرا إلى اللفظ

RAZI-FULL:v29p81/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p81/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p81/r1.claim: “Do not diminish the balance” means do not reduce the measured object.
RAZI-FULL:v29p81/r1.anchor: ولا تخسروا الميزان } أي لا تنقصوا الموزون

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r2.claim: The subjunctive warns against tyranny and oppression; the imperative warns against withholding what is due to another.
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r2.anchor: the first indicates that one must not be tyrannical and oppressive; the second indicates that one must not withhold what is due to another (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.claim: Repeating the Balance three times underscores justice as fundamental to divine creation and human transactions.
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.anchor: the fact that it is here thrice mentioned indicates the fundamental importance of justice

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that the heavens and earth are founded on justice; no grading is given.
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.anchor: The Prophet is reported to have said,“The heavens and the earth are founded upon justice.”

TAB-FULL:v22p179/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r1.claim: Do not reduce weights when weighing for others or wrong them.
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r1.anchor: حدثني يونس قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب قال: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان} [الرحمن: 9]

TAB-FULL:v22p179/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas warns the Mawali to fear God when measuring or weighing: even a small shortfall ruined earlier people, while God may add without loss to the honest measure.
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {والسماء رفعها ووضع الميزان ألا تطغوا في الميزان وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان} [الرحمن: 8] قال قتادة: قال ابن عباس: «يا معشر الموالي إنكم وليتم أمرين

TAB-FULL:v22p179/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd explains that reducing the balance means causing a loss by making the weight deficient.
TAB-FULL:v22p179/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان} [الرحمن: 9] قال: «نقصه

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r7.claim: The following command to establish fair weight and not diminish the balance supports taking the preceding words as a prohibition against transgression.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r7.anchor:
ويدل عليه المعطوف عليه وهو قوله:
(وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان (9)

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r8.claim: The transmitted reading has ḍamma on the tāʾ; Arabic allows both akhsartu al-mīzān and khasirtu al-mīzān, with the latter corresponding to the form in the verse.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r8.anchor: القراءة بضم التاء، وروى أهل اللغة: أخسرت الميزان وخسرت، فعلى

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r9.claim: Do not adopt the alternative reading without a sound report from a recognized reading authority; an unnamed early reader was not a source for recitation.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r9.anchor:
ولا تقرأن بها إلا أن تثبت رواية صحيحة عن إمام في القراءة.
وقد روي أن إنسانا قرأ بها من المتقدمين

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r5.claim: The balance here most likely means the ordinary scale: the command explains its institution by requiring fair weight and forbidding excess or short measure.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r5.anchor: الخ على تقدير أن يراد بالميزان في الآية السابقة أيضا ميزان الأثقال،

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r6.claim: If the earlier balance means any standard of truth or justice, fair weighing is a specific consequence of the general rule.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r6.anchor: وعلى تقدير أن يراد به مطلق التقدير الحق أو العدل هو استخراج حكم جزئي من حكم كلي

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r7.claim: The author reads أن as explanatory, لا تطغوا as prohibition, أقيموا as a coordinated command, and لا تخسروا as a second prohibition reinforcing the first; qist is justice and shortchanging can harm either buyer or seller.

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r8.claim: Reading أن as a subjunctive purpose clause meaning lest you transgress requires a strained account of coordinating commands with a statement.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r8.anchor: نفيا، والتقدير لئلا تطغوا، فيحتاج إلى تكلف توجيه في عطف الإنشاء على الإخبار

TABRISI:55:1-13/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r1.claim: In the related expression about ambushes, the preposition can mean “in” or “at” every ambush.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r1.anchor: أي في كل مرصد أو على كل مرصد وأما تخسروا بفتح التاء

TABRISI:55:1-13/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r2.claim: The form “you diminish” follows the intransitive “the scale lost”; the common form means “I caused it to lose,” though both forms may be used.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r2.anchor: فعلى خسرت الميزان وإنما المشهور أخسرته تقول خسر الميزان

TABRISI:55:6-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:6-10/r12.claim: Establish the scale's tongue fairly when giving or receiving, avoid shortchanging, and level it with fairness.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r12.anchor: أي أقيموا لسان الميزان بالعدل إذا أردتم الأخذ والإعطاء

TABRISI:55:6-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r13.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
TABRISI:55:6-10/r13.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says the scale is established by hand while fairness is established in the heart.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r13.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة الإقامة باليد والقسط بالقلب

THALABI:v9p177#3/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p177#3/r11.claim: The prohibition on transgression means not to incline toward injustice or go beyond the truth in weighing.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r11.anchor: ألا تطغوا يعني لئلا تميلوا وتظلموا وتجاوزوا الحق في الميزان

THALABI:v9p177#3/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r12.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v9p177#3/r12.claim: Abu Darda interprets establishing the weight justly as keeping the scale's tongue level.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r12.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء: أقيموا لسان الميزان بالقسط

THALABI:v9p177#3/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r13.speaker: ابن عيينة
THALABI:v9p177#3/r13.claim: Ibn Uyayna says the hand establishes the scale while the heart establishes justice.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عيينة: الإقامة باليد والقسط بالقلب

THALABI:v9p177#3/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p177#3/r14.claim: Do not lessen the measure, cheat in buying, or shortchange weight.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r14.anchor: ولا تخسروا ولا تنقصوا الميزان ولا تطففوا في الكيل والوزن

THALABI:v9p177#3/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r15.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v9p177#3/r15.claim: Qatada exhorts each person to be fair as they want fairness for themselves and to give full measure, since justice preserves society.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r15.anchor: قال قتادة في هذه الآية: اعدل يا بن آدم كما تحب أن يعدل عليك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās says not to transgress in the balance means not to cheat the person for whom one weighs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r1.anchor: يريد لا تخونوا من وزنتم له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Zajjāj gloss transgressing as wronging, reducing, or exceeding the limit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r2.anchor: لا تظلموا ولا تنقصوا ولا تجاوزوا القدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r3.claim: The warning addresses deliberate short measure; unavoidable imprecision is excused, while intentional loss is transgression, and the repeated noun makes the ban stand independently rather than hang on the preceding construction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r3.anchor: ما لا يضبط في الوزن موضوع عنهم ما لم يتعمدوا البخس فإذا تعمدوا فقد طغوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r4.claim: The commentators say to establish the weighing with equity means to set the scale’s beam straight fairly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r4.anchor: أقيموا لسان الميزان بالقسط، أي: بالعدل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r5.claim: When weighing, first straighten the beam as commanded, then one may voluntarily give more if one wishes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r5.anchor: والأحسن إذا وزن أن يقيم اللسان بالقسط كما أمر الله تعالى ثم يرجح إن أراد ذلك وتبرع به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r6.speaker: علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r6.claim: A report says ʿAlī saw a man weighing saffron with extra; he tipped the scale and told him to weigh evenly first, then give extra as he wished.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138#2/r6.anchor: أقم الوزن بالقسط ثم أرجح بعد ذلك ما شئت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and the commentators gloss not to short-change the balance as not diminishing or cheating.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r1.anchor: ابن عباس والمفسرون: لا تنقصوا # ولا تبخسوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r2.claim: The warning matches the description of people who short-weight others and the prohibition on reducing a measure and balance elsewhere.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r2.anchor: وهذا كقوله تعالى ذكره {وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون} [المطففين: 3] أي ينقصون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r3.claim: Language scholars recognize both akhsartu and khasartuhu for making the balance deficient; Bilāl ibn Abī Burda reads the verse with fatḥa on tāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r3.anchor: أهل اللغة: أخسرت الميزان وخسرته ومنه قراءة بلال بن أبي بردة (¬2) {ولا تخسروا} بفتح التاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p139/r4.claim: The same meaning appears in the instruction not to reduce the measure and balance in the address to Midian.

ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r3.claim: People must weigh their deeds fairly and must not fall short of the measure.
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r3.anchor: weigh, therefore, [your deed] with equity, and cut not the measure short!

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r2.claim: He renders the command as keeping the weighing straight with justice and not diminishing the balance.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r2.anchor: doğru tutun adaletle tartıyı da aksatmayın mîzânı

ELMALILI:55:1-13#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13#3/r2.claim: People must weigh words and deeds fairly, use full measures, and judge with the same standard for themselves and others; they must not misuse the scales or ruin their afterlife scale.
ELMALILI:55:1-13#3/r2.anchor: hem vezni, kavil ve fiil her hususta tartmak işini adaletle doğru tutun

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r16.claim: Justice is the basic principle for preserving balance, while fair conduct in concrete human affairs requires care, good-faith judgment, and full effort.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r16.anchor: Beşerî ilişkiler bakımından bunun adı “hakkaniyet”tir. Bunu belirlemede kişilere düşen, takdir yetkisini iyi niyet esasına dayalı olarak kullanmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r17.claim: For duties toward God, justice is realized by following revelation without adding anything of one's own to religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r17.anchor: kişinin dine kendisinden bir şey katmadan ilâhî bildirime uygun davranmasıyla mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r18.claim: The use of qist, meaning fairness, with weighing and scales shows that justice and universal balance must be enacted in lived situations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r18.anchor: “hakkaniyet” anlamına gelen “kıst” kelimesine yer verilmesi burada vezin ve mîzan kelimelerinin adalet ilkesinin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r19.claim: Do not diminish the measure can also mean acting so that one's deeds do not tip the afterlife scales against oneself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r19.anchor: her bir olayla ilgili uygulamanın yani bütün davranışlarımızın âhiretteki teraziyi aleyhimize çevirmeyecek biçimde olması gerektiği şeklinde de yorumlanabilir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.claim: The first signs emphasized show that God cherishes justice and rejects whatever violates justice and equity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.anchor: First and foremost are mentioned those signs and manifestations which point to the fact that the Almighty greatly cherishes justice and does not approve anything contrary to justice and equity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r3.claim: Honest weighing and measuring apply the cosmic principle in daily life; cheating is social disorder and attacks the foundation of the world God built.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r3.anchor: they should weigh and measure with full honesty and not weigh less. While commenting on the anecdote of the Prophet Shu‘ayb’s people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p115/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p115/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p115/r1.claim: The Qur’an uses positive and negative formulations when disobedience has dangerous consequences, underscoring the great significance of just weighing and measuring.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p115/r1.anchor: this style is adopted at instances when not obeying the real directive can lead to very dangerous consequences.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p115/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p115/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p115/r2.claim: A society or nation that disrupts the command to weigh justly creates disorder throughout society.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p115/r2.anchor: a nation which disrupts and disobeys this directive creates disorder in the whole society.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r8.claim: Because fairness is important, God commands just weighing; the common أخسر reading means damage or reduce, as in the warning about sellers diminishing measures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r8.anchor: ولما كانت التسوية مطلوبة جدا، أمر الله تعالى فقال: وأقيموا الوزن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r9.speaker: بلال بن أبي بردة وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r9.claim: They read تخسر with open tāʾ from خسر, with the same meaning; other readings open tāʾ and vary the sīn vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r9.anchor: وبلال بن أبي بردة وزيد بن علي: تخسر بفتح التاء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r10.claim: He explains a reading by deleting في before الميزان; Abu Hayyan says this is unnecessary because خسر takes a direct object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r10.anchor: وخرجها الزمخشري على أن يكون التقدير: في الميزان، فحذف الجار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r11.claim: After forbidding excess, the verse forbids reduction; repeating الميزان reinforces the recommendation and strengthens the command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r11.anchor: لما منع من الزيادة، وهي الطغيان، نهى عن الخسران الذي هو نقصان،

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r1.claim: The command means to perform weighing justly; al-Raghib broadens it to fairness in all human actions and speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r1.anchor: قوموا وزنكم بالعدل وقال الراغب : هذا إشارة إلى مراعاة المعدلة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says to level the balance's beam when buying and selling; Sufyan ibn Uyayna says fairness is enacted by the hand and grounded in the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهدأن المعنى أقيموا لسان الميزان بالعدل إذا أردتم الأخذ والإعطاء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r3.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says the balance is set correctly by the hand, while equity resides in the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r3.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة : الإقامة باليد والقسط بالقلب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r4.claim: The command coordinates with the preceding negated clause despite its imperative form, since it can be read as a verbal noun; another makes the earlier la prohibitive for parallelism.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r4.anchor: ولا يضر في ذلك كونها إنشائية وتلك خبرية لأنها لتأويلها بالمفرد تجردت عن معنى الطلب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r5.claim: Do not reduce the balance: its proper function is to make measurements equal; repeating the word reinforces the instruction and urge to use it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r5.anchor: أي لا تنقصوه فإن منحقه أن يسوي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r6.claim: Several readings vary the vowels of the verb “reduce”; Zayd ibn Ali and Bilal ibn Abi Burda read with an open first vowel and kasra on the sīn.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r6.anchor: وقرأزيد بن علي وبلال بن أبي بردة بفتح التاء وكسر السين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari analyzes a reading as originally requiring a preposition that was deleted; Abu Hayyan objects that the verb is independently transitive, so deletion is unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r7.anchor: وخرج ذلك الزمخشري على أن الأصل ولا تخسروا في الميزان فحذف الجار

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan says the verb can take an object directly, citing Quranic usage, so there is no need to posit a deleted preposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r8.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان بأن خسر قد جاء متعدياكقوله تعالى : ( خسروا أنفسهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r9.claim: One explanation makes the loss concern the afterlife: failure to honor the balance leaves people losers on Judgment Day; al-Raghib says both worldly fairness and avoiding that loss are intended and interrelated.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r9.anchor: أي لا تخسروا أنفسكم في الميزان أي لا تكونوا خاسرين يوم القيامة بسبب الميزان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r10.claim: Another account supplies an omitted noun for what is weighed, or uses “balance” figuratively for the weighed object.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102#2/r10.anchor: بتقدير مضاف أي موزون الميزان أو جعل الميزان مجازاعن الموزون فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Darda and Ata explain the command as leveling the balance's tongue justly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء وعطاء: معناه أقيموا لسان الميزان بالعدل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r7.speaker: ابن عيينة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r7.claim: Ibn Uyayna says establishing the scale is by the hand, while justice is in the heart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عيينة: الإقامة باليد والقسط بالقلب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r8.claim: Do not diminish the scale or defraud in measure or weight.

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r6.claim: Set weight fairly and do not diminish the balance, since fairness is its purpose; repetition intensifies the exhortation and several vocalizations are reported.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r6.anchor: ولا تنقصوه فإن من حقه أن يسوى لأنه المقصود من وضعه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r6.claim: People must make all their actions conform to justice and must not diminish any instrument of justice, including measure, weight, judgment, or quantity; repeated mention stresses the command’s gravity.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r6.anchor: من الذرع والوزن والعدل والكيل ونحو - نوعا من أنواع الخسر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.claim: The balance includes every instrument for weighing or measuring quantities; God placed it on earth for judgments, transactions, and the fair treatment He enjoined in giving and taking.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.anchor: وأراد به كل ما توزن به الأشياء وتعرف مقاديرها من ميزان وقرسطون ومكيال ومقياس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r20.claim: The command is to weigh justly and the prohibition is against both unjust excess and short measure; repeating “the balance” strengthens the admonition and the command to use it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r20.anchor: أمر بالتسوية ونهى عن الطغيان الذي هو اعتداء وزيادة ، وعن الخسران الذي هو تطفيف ونقصان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r22.claim: The verb in “do not give short measure” has readings with fatḥa on tāʾ and with ḍamma, kasra, or fatḥa on sīn; the fatḥa analysis deletes the preposition fī from the underlying phrase.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r22.anchor: بفتح التاء وضم السين وكسرها وفتحها
